the only difference is `--merge-synonyms`: - **Before**: `no_merge_id` (no synonym merging) - **After**: `new_merge_id` (`--merge-synonyms`) | | Before | After | |-----------------------------------|:------:|:-----:| | IS names | 36 | 32 | | Loci | 45 | 45 | | Copies (sum of `copy_number`) | 67 | 67 | | Stitched loci | 5 | 6 | | IS names found in more than 1 locus | 7 | 9 | : Overview {.striped} ### Stitched IS | IS | Before | After | Copy number | Contigs in the path | |--------|:------:|:-----:|:-----------:|---------------------------------------------| | IS1397 | ✓ | ✓ | 2 | 1241248, 1234872, 1208211, 1015060, 1244160, 1245026 | | IS1F | ✓ | ✓ | 2 | 1158833, 1202947, 1244706 | | ISEc23 | ✓ | ✓ | 3 | 1116087, 1244816, 1176191, 1245048 | | ISEc52 | ✓ | ✓ | 3 | 1243586, 1245082, 238677 | | ISEc8 | ✓ | ✓ | 2 | 1236644, 1235120, 1125059, 1240608 | | **IS1A** | ✗ | **✓** | 3 | 1171599, 1245138, 1208153, 1245038 | : The 5 IS stitched before are stitched along exactly the same paths after; merging adds IS1A {.striped} - IS1A only stitches after merging because, before, its pieces had different names: IS1A (1171599), IS1R (1208153), IS1G (1245138) and IS1B (1245136). Stitching only joins pieces with the same name. ### Names that changed after merging | Before | After | Loci before → after | Copies before → after | |--------------------------------|--------|:-------------------:|:---------------------:| | IS1A, IS1B, IS1G, IS1R | IS1A | 4 → 4 | 9 → 9 | | IS1203, IS629 | IS3411 | 2 → 2 | 2 → 2 | | ISSd1 | IS600 | 1 → 1 | 2 → 2 | | IS21 | IS640 | 1 → 1 | 1 → 1 | : Merging renames IS to the first name found, which is not always the truth name (ISSd1 and IS21 are the names in the truth file) {.striped} - Merging only renames: the number of loci and copies stays the same for every IS. ### Same name but not stitched (after merging) | IS | Loci | Stitched | Not stitched | Coverage of unstitched loci | Copies | Truth | Why | |---------|:----:|:--------:|:------------:|-----------------------------|:------:|:-----:|-----------------------------| | IS1A | 4 | 1 | 3 | 37%, 58%, 58% | 9 | 3 | leftover pieces (duplicates) | | IS1F | 3 | 1 | 2 | 42%, 44% | 5 | 2 | leftover pieces; the 44% on 1244320 is likely the real 2nd copy | | ISEc23 | 3 | 1 | 2 | 52%, 45% | 9 | 3 | leftover pieces (duplicates) | | ISEc52 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 52% | 5 | 3 | leftover piece (duplicate) | | ISEc8 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 45% | 3 | 1 | leftover piece (duplicate) | | IS200C | 2 | 0 | 2 | 70%, 70% | 2 | 2 | real separate copies | | IS3411 | 2 | 0 | 2 | 80%, 40% | 2 | 2 | real separate copies | | IS609 | 2 | 0 | 2 | 31%, 68% | 2 | 2 | real separate copies | | MITEEc1 | 2 | 0 | 2 | 100%, 100% | 2 | 2 | real separate copies | : 9 IS names are found in more than one locus: 4 are real separate copies, 5 have 9 leftover pieces that were not stitched {.striped} - Every leftover piece is partial, and sits on a contig inside the stitched path or one contig away from it. - Before merging, 7 IS names were found in more than one locus, with 6 leftover pieces (IS1F 2, ISEc23 2, ISEc52 1, ISEc8 1). IS1A and IS3411 were not in that list because their loci had different names (IS1A/IS1B/IS1G/IS1R and IS1203/IS629). ## Other Problem found ::: {#f4897c56 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # see if the synonyms merging was working print(df[(df["target"].str.startswith("IS1A", na=False)) & (df["context"] == "INSIDE")]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` locus_id target gene_id \ 45 locus_split_a13a8928 IS1A_IS1_unknown_stitched 1171599_2_173 46 locus_split_a13a8928 IS1A_IS1_unknown_stitched 1245138_99_444 47 locus_split_a13a8928 IS1A_IS1_unknown_stitched 1208153_0_267 49 locus_split_a13a8928 IS1A_IS1_unknown_stitched 1245038_99340_99433 57 locus_c482ac96 IS1A_IS1_unknown 1208153_0_267 291 locus_8639f554 IS1A_IS1_unknown 1245136_1_181 292 locus_8639f554 IS1A_IS1_unknown 1245136_225_444 296 locus_127d15b0 IS1A_IS1_unknown 1245138_99_444 context dist_bp topo_hops orientation effect copy_number \ 45 INSIDE 0 0 opposite strand NONE 3.0 46 INSIDE 0 0 same strand NONE 3.0 47 INSIDE 0 0 same strand NONE 3.0 49 INSIDE 0 0 same strand NONE 3.0 57 INSIDE 0 0 same strand NONE 3.0 291 INSIDE 0 0 same strand NONE 1.0 292 INSIDE 0 0 same strand NONE 1.0 296 INSIDE 0 0 same strand NONE 2.0 locus_contig locus_start locus_end coverage_pct 45 1171599|1245138|1208153|1245038 0 99436 48.4 46 1171599|1245138|1208153|1245038 0 99436 48.4 47 1171599|1245138|1208153|1245038 0 99436 48.4 49 1171599|1245138|1208153|1245038 0 99436 48.4 57 1208153 0 282 36.7 291 1245136 0 447 58.2 292 1245136 0 447 58.2 296 1245138 0 447 58.2 ``` ::: ::: There are: - 3 locus and 5 copies in total for IS1F (supposed to be only 2 copies) - 4 locus and 8 copies in total for IS1A (supposed to be 3) **This because after we stitched the IS together, the pipeline didn't removed the rest of the nodes which make a duplicate copies** ## Calculating the precision and recall Two comparisons against the truth BED: - name only - with copy number Each is done without and with synonyms. With synonyms, names that ISfinder lists as synonyms/isoforms (e.g. IS30 / IS30D) count as the same IS, so a different name for the same element is not counted as a miss. ::: {#69db885f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} from eris.synonyms import SynonymResolver, fetch_isfinder_table synonyms = SynonymResolver(fetch_isfinder_table()) loci = pd.read_csv("../result/new_merge_id/new_merge_id_report.tsv", sep="\t").drop_duplicates("locus_id") truth = pd.read_csv("../../data/ec958_IS.reannotated.sorted.bed", sep="\t", header=None)[3] truth = truth[truth.str.split("_").str[0] != "ISSen10"] # ISSen10 excluded from the truth set def is_name(name, use_synonyms): # IS1A_IS1_unknown_stitched / IS1A_2 -> IS1A; with synonyms, every synonym gets the same name return (synonyms.canonical(name) if use_synonyms else name).split("_")[0] def copies_per_is(use_synonyms): eris = loci.groupby(loci["target"].map(lambda n: is_name(n, use_synonyms)))["copy_number"].sum() real = truth.map(lambda n: is_name(n, use_synonyms)).value_counts() return pd.concat([real.rename("truth"), eris.rename("eris")], axis=1).fillna(0).astype(int) # IS where eris and the truth disagree (with synonyms) counts = copies_per_is(use_synonyms=True) counts[counts["truth"] != counts["eris"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {#2baf46ee .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} rows, errors = [], {} for use_synonyms in (False, True): counts = copies_per_is(use_synonyms) for mode in ("name only", "with copy number"): c = counts.clip(upper=1) if mode == "name only" else counts tp = c.min(axis=1).sum() fp = (c["eris"] - c["truth"]).clip(lower=0).sum() fn = (c["truth"] - c["eris"]).clip(lower=0).sum() precision, recall = tp / (tp + fp), tp / (tp + fn) rows.append({"Synonyms": use_synonyms, "Comparison": mode, "TP": tp, "FP": fp, "FN": fn, "Precision": round(precision, 3), "Recall": round(recall, 3), "F1": round(2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall), 3)}) # Which IS are wrong: "FP 6" = eris has 6 too many, "FN 1" = eris misses 1 diff = c["eris"] - c["truth"] errors[(f"synonyms={use_synonyms}", mode)] = diff[diff != 0].map( lambda d: f"FP {d}" if d > 0 else f"FN {-d}") display(pd.DataFrame(rows)) pd.DataFrame(errors).fillna("").sort_index() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
